- **Flagship-protection rule:** BYO sum to reach Signature's configuration must price ≥ 1.25× Signature's `+$B`, and BYO sum to reach Elite's configuration must price ≥ 1.35× Elite's `+$C`. Flagships remain the rational discount for anyone wanting that full stack.

You're describing **pure SaaS** — software that's already modular by design. Freemium/Pro/Enterprise is already a tiered structure, and seat-based pricing is already a configuration dimension. There's no service delivery to atomize, no consulting hours to decompose into deliverables, no done-for-you work to package.

Intelligent-clay exists to turn *human-delivered services* (consulting, coaching, agencies, done-for-you work) into productized, configurable offerings. That transformation problem doesn't apply to you — your product is already the clay's finished form.

**What you likely want instead:**

- **Packaging/pricing strategy for SaaS** — feature-tier design, value-metric selection (seats vs. usage vs. outcomes), fence-building between tiers. Frameworks: Kyle Poyar (OpenView), Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell), *Monetizing Innovation* (Ramanujam & Tacke).
- **Enterprise plan structuring** — turning "custom" into a real menu (modules, usage bands, SLAs, support tiers). This is closest to what I do, but for the *services wrapper* around Enterprise (onboarding, CSM, professional services), not the software itself.
- **Feature-to-tier assignment** — Jobs-to-be-Done or segmentation work to decide what lives in Free vs. Pro vs. Enterprise.

**One place I could actually help:** if your Enterprise plan includes significant **professional services** — implementation, custom integrations, training, dedicated CSM, migration work — that services layer *is* clay and I can productize it into modular Enterprise add-ons with BYO configuration. If that's a real part of your revenue, describe that layer and I'll run the skill on it.

Otherwise, this needs a SaaS pricing/packaging resource, not this one.

This skill doesn't apply here.

Handmade leather wallets are a **physical product**, not a service. There's nothing to atomize into time blocks, access tiers, or support levels. Modularizing this belongs to **SKU and bundle logic**, not service productization.

## What you actually want

**1. SKU variants** — one product, configurable axes:
- *Leather:* vegetable-tanned / chromexcel / shell cordovan (price ladder)
- *Style:* bifold / cardholder / long wallet / zip
- *Card slots:* 4 / 6 / 8
- *Thread color, edge finish, monogram*

**2. Bundles** — wallet + cardholder + keychain at a bundled discount.

**3. Tiered product lines** — Everyday ($120) / Signature ($220, premium leather) / Bespoke ($450+, made-to-order with monogram and leather choice).

**4. A product configurator** — Shopify has native variant logic; for deeper customization use a builder app (Kickflip, Zakeke, Product Options & Customizer).

## When this skill *would* apply

If you added a **service layer** around the wallets — e.g.:
- *Custom design consultations* (30-min call → bespoke wallet spec)
- *Leather goods workshops* (teach customers to make their own)
- *Corporate gifting service* (bulk custom orders with branding, account management, reorder cadence)
- *Repair & restoration service*

Any of those are services and could be modularized into tiers + build-your-own. Want to go that direction? Name the service layer and I'll run the full blueprint.

## Part 3 — Three Tiers + Build-Your-Own

### Tier 1 — **Clay Open** (Free / MIT)
- **Configuration:** Depth: Core skill only · Breadth: Markdown-only · Support: Community · Deployment: Personal · License: MIT · Memory: None or claude-mem local · Iteration: Manual pulls
- **Positioning:** For the solo consultant or curious builder who wants to productize their own offering using the raw skill.
- **Pricing logic:** $0. Anchor is the existing open-source repo — this tier is the funnel, not the revenue. Its job is adoption breadth and credibility.

### Tier 2 — **Clay Pro** *(flagship)* — `+$A/mo` or `+$A×12` annual
- **Configuration:** Depth: Core + 2 vertical packs of choice · Breadth: +Configurator export (JSON/YAML) · Support: Async blueprint review (2/mo) + monthly group office hours · Deployment: Personal or up to 3 seats · License: Commercial internal · Memory: claude-mem local · Iteration: GitHub Action
- **Positioning:** For the working consultant/coach actively productizing 1–5 offerings who needs export formats, a second pair of eyes, and commercial-use rights.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against the cost of one hour of the buyer's own billable time × ~2 (they save >2 hours in the first run). Sits well below any bespoke productization consultant engagement (which would be $5–15K per offering).

### Tier 3 — **Clay Studio** — `+$B/mo` or annual contract
- **Configuration:** Depth: Core + all vertical packs + custom dimension authoring · Breadth: Full platform integrations (Notion, Airtable, Typeform, custom webhooks) · Support: Weekly group office hours + dedicated Slack Connect · Deployment: Team seats (up to 10) or white-label · License: White-label + resale · Memory: Hosted memory service · Iteration: Managed updates
- **Positioning:** For agencies productizing client offerings at scale, or platforms embedding Clay into their own product (course platforms, agency-ops tools, coaching marketplaces).
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against (a) one seat of comparable agency-ops tooling × team size, and (b) the alternative of building this in-house (3–6 months of one engineer). Priced so a 5-person agency recoups it after productizing 2 client offerings.
